column11: ANCHOR, a measured analogue: the share of US uncomplicated malaria treated with Coartem, the first and only artemisinin combination approved in the US (April 2009). In 2018, 'artemether-lumefantrine for 213 (16.4%)' of 1,296 patients with medications recorded, behind atovaquone-proguanil at 789 (60.9%) (Malaria Surveillance, United States, 2018, MMWR Surveill Summ 2022;71(SS-8)); in 2017, 200 (12.8%) of 1,567 (Malaria Surveillance, United States, 2017, MMWR Surveill Summ 2021;70(SS-2)), so it was still climbing nine years after approval. MULTIPLE 0.5, A JUDGEMENT: 0.5 x 16.4% = 8.2%
column12: the most arguable figure here. Against: GanLum (KLU156), Novartis's own non-artemisinin combination, positive in Phase 3 and due for submission in 2026, would reach the same patients first; generic atovaquone-proguanil takes six in ten US courses; artemisinin partial resistance is an African problem that rarely changes a US traveller's treatment; and two thirds of these patients are treated in hospital, where a single-dose cure saves little. For more: a single-dose cure active against resistant parasites, and the 16.4% share counts all species, where chloroquine (7.0%) serves only the non-falciparum cases
